fix: Public builder panics on app-author input without the paired form the repo requires. Add `#[must_use] pub fn maybe_pressures(mut self, start: f32, peak: f32) -> Option<Self>` (or a typed error enum) that returns None when `!(peak > start)`, and make `pressures` a documented wrapper that calls `.expect("peak pressure exceeds start pressure")` on it.

Dispatch clones the KeyboardEvent up to three times per key press (lines 43, 50, 58); keyboard_types' Key::Character holds a String, so each clone allocates for character keys. Change the callback types (on_shortcut, on_key, on_key_down, on_key_repeat, on_key_up in details.rs) to take `&KeyboardEvent` and pass `&event` here, removing every `event.clone()`.

Each shortcut match allocates an Rc and clones the command (a String for the default Command) per key event. Build the ErasedIntent once when the shortcut is bound (store it in the shortcut map next to the intent) so `find_match` clones an Rc. If the binding stays as-is, at least avoid re-erasing per event.

Every invoke of an action with an invocation listener allocates two Vecs (Start and End). Store the listeners as `RefCell<Rc<[Weak<ActionInvocationListenerEntry>]>>`, rebuilt copy-on-write on subscribe and drop (rare), and have notify clone the Rc (no allocation) before releasing the borrow. This keeps the 'added during delivery waits' rule. The same applies to notify_action_listeners (line 402).

Keyboard action dispatch clones the command to rebuild an Intent for lookup (a String allocation for the default Command). Add an `&C`-keyed lookup on Actions, e.g. `invoke_command_first(&self, command: &C) -> Option<ActionResult>`, that walks scopes with `scope.actions.get(command)` and calls `action.invoke(action.intent())`. Use it here, and in `Actions::invoke` (line 625, `self.invoke_intent(&Intent::new(command.clone()))`), which has the same clone.
